question: What physical quantities can be precisely measured using a levitated nanosphere?

ingredients.name: answer_critical_0
ingredients.criterion: The answer identifies force and torque as the physical quantities that can be precisely measured with a levitated nanosphere (ultrasensitive force detection via center-of-mass motion; torque via rotational degrees of freedom, e.g., a levitated nanorotor).
examples: Levitated nanospheres serve as ultrasensitive force and torque sensors
A levitated nanorotor exploits rotational degrees of freedom for torque measurement

ingredients.name: answer_critical_1
ingredients.criterion: The answer cites the achieved force metrics: sensitivity of 6.33 ± 1.62 zN/Hz^1/2 (optimal 4.34 zN/Hz^1/2) and resolution of 166.40 ± 55.48 yN at the optimal measurement time of 2751 s.
examples: A force resolution of 166.40 ± 55.48 yN was achieved at 2751 s

ingredients.name: answer_critical_2
ingredients.criterion: The answer cites the torque sensitivity of (4.2 ± 1.2) × 10^-27 N m Hz^-1/2, achieved at room temperature, outperforming the best cryogenic torsion-based torque sensor (2.9 × 10^-24 N m Hz^-1/2) without complex nanofabrication.
examples: Torque sensitivity of (4.2 ± 1.2) × 10^-27 N m Hz^-1/2 at room temperature
Two orders of magnitude better than the cryogenic torsion balance record

ingredients.name: valuable_0
ingredients.criterion: The answer mentions that the nanoparticle's rotational frequency can be measured or exploited, with record speeds beyond 5 GHz (300 billion rpm), relevant to torque sensing.
examples: The nanorotor spins beyond 5 GHz (300 billion rpm)
Record-high rotation speeds enable ultrasensitive torque sensing

ingredients.name: valuable_1
ingredients.criterion: The answer attributes the precision to ultrahigh-vacuum levitation (e.g., 7.9 × 10^-9 mbar), low mass, environmental isolation, and suppression of thermal noise and residual gas collisions.
examples: Ultrahigh vacuum (7.9 × 10^-9 mbar) suppresses collisions with residual gas molecules
Low mass and environmental isolation make levitated particles suitable for ultrasensitive detection

ingredients.name: valuable_2
ingredients.criterion: The answer mentions that parametric feedback cooling (e.g., CoM cooled to ~1.98 mK) and the Allan variance method for assessing stability and determining the optimal measurement time underlie the force precision.
examples: Parametric feedback cooling cooled the center of mass to about 2 mK
The Allan variance was minimized to determine the optimal measurement time for resolution

ingredients.name: valuable_3
ingredients.criterion: The answer compares the levitated system favorably to conventional sensors, such as cryogenic torsion balances and complex nanofabricated sensors.
examples: Surpasses the most sensitive cryogenic torque sensors at room temperature

ingredients.name: valuable_4
ingredients.criterion: The answer connects the measurements to applications such as fifth-force searches, gravitational wave detection, dark matter research, vacuum friction, Casimir effect, quantum geometric phase, or nanoscale magnetism.
examples: Force sensing enables searches for fifth forces, dark matter, and high-frequency gravitational waves
The nanorotor could detect vacuum friction and study nanoscale magnetism

ingredients.name: valuable_5
ingredients.criterion: The answer directly addresses the question by naming the quantities (force and torque) rather than only discussing techniques or applications.
examples: The answer explicitly states that force and torque can be precisely measured
The quantities measured are named upfront, with numbers as supporting detail
